summary: Randomized 2x2 classroom experiment (N=132 CS1 students, Python) comparing four GPT-4o AI teaching-assistant configurations: Socratic vs direct guidance, and with vs without the problem statement and student code as context. The Socratic + full-context TA was rated significantly lower for helping complete tasks; other differences (stress, external LLM use, comprehension) were descriptive and non-significant.

claims.claim: Students rated the Socratic + Full Context AI TA lowest for perceived task-completion support.
claims.evidence: §4.1: Kruskal-Wallis chi2(3)=12.14, p=.007; mean 3.53 vs 4.12-4.27 in other cells. Only an omnibus test is reported; no post-hoc pairwise test (e.g. Dunn) isolates which cell differs.

claims.claim: This condition had the highest external LLM use, stress, and lowest comprehension.
claims.evidence: §4.2.1: 23% (7/30) vs 9-15%, chi2(3)=2.47, p=.48; stress p=.213; full comprehension 48% vs 67% (descriptive, no test). Authors acknowledge non-significance in the abstract.

claims.claim: Lack of context makes students write longer messages; Socratic + no context drives more queries.
claims.evidence: §4.2.2: queries per problem 11.1 vs 4.1-5.1, chi2(3)=13.28, p=.004; message length 126 vs 54-81 chars, chi2(3)=29.96, p<.001.

patterns.note: Prompt-level pedagogical guardrails (not policy-as-code) can create friction that pushes users to unrestricted external LLMs; tangential to agent permission guardrails.

methodology.sample: 132 analyzed of 598 enrolled / 254 interested; 30-37 per cell; three simple Python tasks (prime check, duplicate detection, matrix neighbor sum).
methodology.baselines: Factorial comparison of four prompt configurations; no no-AI control.
methodology.variance: Non-parametric omnibus tests; no effect sizes or post-hoc pairwise tests reported.
methodology.contamination_controls: n/a; function names anonymized to limit solution inference.

standards.peer_review: arXiv preprint; no venue listed (CCS-formatted, likely a computing-education submission).
standards.artifacts: No code, prompts, or data released.

biases.detail: Volunteers for 0.5% extra credit; 132 of 254 interested students retained after exclusions, causing cell imbalance.
30-37 students per cell; comprehension measured on one task.
Ceiling effect: 128/132 passed all tests (mean 2.98/3), so task success cannot discriminate conditions; outcomes rest on self-report Likert items.
About student-facing tutoring chatbots, not software-engineering agents or harnesses.

coi.affiliations: University of Florida; University of Auckland.
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: GPT-4o used as backend; the coding platform resembles the authors' prior system (Kapoor et al., 2026).
coi.funding: No acknowledgments or funding statement found.

verdict_reason: off-topic: classroom RCT on AI teaching-assistant prompt design for CS1 students, not LLM agents for software engineering or harness design; also omnibus-only statistics with most headline differences non-significant.
applicability: Does not inform the agentic harness. At most a product-side note for a team delivering healthcare-education content to front ends: if that content is later fronted by a tutoring chatbot, rigid Socratic guardrails combined with full context were rated least helpful and may push learners to external tools. Nothing transfers to Java backend ingestion, ≥4-repo coordination, mixed agent hosts, or spec-driven development.
